I have been doing this for forty years on this same land in Quzhou. My mother farmed before me. I do not need to think too hard — my hands know what to do.

My two mu goes to wheat first, then maize. Same ground, same routine, same as always. I split the land evenly in my head but it is all one field, just different times of year.

**Wheat (October to June):** I will buy the same improved wheat seed I bought last year from the village seed shop — I do not remember the name but the owner knows what I always take. I will rotary-till after the maize is off the field and spread compound fertilizer before seeding, then top-dress urea after the New Year when it starts to green up. I water four times: once before it gets cold to help roots settle, once at jointing, once at heading, once when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide in the fall and then again in spring if the weeds come back. I spray fungicide once around heading because some years the rust comes. My wheat usually gives me about 450 jin per mu, sometimes more.

**Maize (June to September):** Right after I cut the wheat I plant maize without ploughing — no time and the ground is already loose enough. I use hybrid seed, the kind everyone in the village uses. I put fertilizer down at planting and top-dress once more around knee-height. Summer gets rain so I only water once or twice if it stays dry in August. I spray herbicide right after planting before the seedlings come up, and watch for corn borer — if I see damage I spray once. Maize gives me about 550 jin per mu in a good year.

My sons send some money home but I still need this grain for the family — seven mouths, and I sell whatever is left over.
